assembly: Every output frame is one complete source drawing. Whole-frame background extraction and size/root registration only. No crossfades, frame mixtures, opacity curves or part deformation.

prompts.purpose: Complete closing and growth poses; source frames 0 through 8 used
prompts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit / fully drawn 2D game animation sprite sheet. Create ONE production sprite sheet with EXACTLY 24 COMPLETE individually painted animation frames arranged in a strict 6-column by 4-row regular grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Large landscape canvas, ideally 3072x2048, every cell square. Input image 1 is the exact original small starting nest; input image 2 is the closed, grown bud; input image 3 is the exact original fully mature final nest. Keep their illustration style and character design: ivory curled petals with mint-green shading, delicate dark-green outlines, golden seed and green sprout, green leaf rosette and curled vine stems. Draw the WHOLE plant in EVERY cell as one finished coherent illustration, including fully resolved petal bases, rear surfaces, leaf overlaps and connected roots. This sheet will directly supply the actual animation frames. Do not provide separated parts, sketches, or a preview mockup. CRITICAL: NO crossfades, NO dissolves, NO semitransparent transitional objects, NO ghost images, NO superimposed before/after pictures. The sprite interior is fully opaque in every cell; only the empty background outside it is transparent. No chopped leaves, no rectangular patches, no floating petal fragments. The same attached petals gather into a closed bud, grow, and then physically bend outward and unfurl, revealing the same seed and sprout. The lower vine stems originate at the central root, gradually lengthen sideways and then curl upward; do not materialize them at the outer edges. Maintain coherent identity, paint marks, leaf count and occlusion across the complete sequence. Fixed front camera, fixed central axis, fixed ground contact at x=50%, y=90.43% in every cell. Keep plenty of transparent padding: initial plant height about 32.8% of cell height and width 48%; adult plant height 56.25% of cell height and final width 64.3%. Do not change adult scale while opening. The adult rear pointed sepal stays at the same top height, and the seed, sprout and central base remain the same size and position once revealed. Timeline by ZERO-BASED frame indices: 0 exactly matches the small open nest reference; 1-3 its same petals curl inward to gather; 4 fully closed small bud; 5-8 the closed bud steadily grows upward from the fixed root; 9 matches the grown closed bud reference; 10 tips begin separating; 11-17 the same attached petals unfold outward in seven clear successive small increments, upper tips first then petal bodies, with completed clean undersides and bases in each drawing; 18 fully open flower body with short vine shoots at the central root; 19-22 its lower stems slowly grow from the center outward and upward while the flower body stays exactly still; 23 precisely matches the mature final reference. All 24 frames must be present, each a complete painted sprite with clean connected roots and natural leaf overlaps. No text, numbers, grid lines, borders, ground lines, arrows, shadows, labels or watermarks. True transparent background, not a painted checkerboard.

prompts.purpose: Complete reverse closing poses used in reverse order for opening
prompts.prompt: Production 2D game animation, fully drawn frames. Create a new sheet with EXACTLY FIFTEEN COMPLETE whole-plant paintings in a 5-column by 3-row grid, read left to right then top to bottom. Image 1 is the EXACT mature nest design and is the binding character reference; image 2 is its completely closed bud. This sequence runs IN REVERSE: start with the mature open flower from image 1 and slowly close that SAME flower into image 2. Frame 0 must match the mature design including its prominent LARGE FRONT HEART-SHAPED IVORY PETAL. This front heart is the third main petal, in front of and below the golden seed; it is not optional. Keep it physically attached throughout the first twelve frames as it folds into the front face of the bud. The nest has a pointed rear sepal, two curled side petals, this broad front heart petal, a small separate ivory heart at the root, green leaf fan, and two curled vine stems. There must never be a two-petal alternative design. Frames 0-3: the complete front heart is broad and plainly visible; it tilts upward slightly while the side petals curl inward a few degrees, and the connected vine stems begin slowly drawing toward the central root. Frames 4-7: the SAME front heart bends upward around the seed and narrows into a cup, its two lobes folding together, while the side petals gather around it; the leaf fan and vine stems retract gradually toward their attached root. Frames 8-11: the front petal is now a tall narrow folded panel, still clearly part of the same bud, with the seed and sprout naturally becoming occluded by the enclosing petals; only shorter curled stem shoots remain at the central root. Frames 12-14: the tips gather and meet, the last seam closes, ending with the full grown closed bud exactly like image 2, standing on four green basal leaves. Keep ALL paintings at the same adult body scale, same front view, same root at horizontal center near the bottom, and same top apex height. The camera does not move. Do not shrink the whole object while closing. This is a single coherent botanical movement, not shape replacement. EVERY frame must be a finished opaque painting with complete clean petal bases and resolved leaf overlaps, no missing surfaces or floating fragments. Keep the exact painterly ivory-and-mint illustration style, dark green contours and original golden seed design. No crossfade, no dissolved parts, no transparency ghosts, no pasted overlays, no separate parts. True transparent background outside the plants, with no halos, haze, gradients, shadows, text, labels, numbers or grid lines. The full plant fits well inside each cell with transparent margins. Output the actual fifteen-frame production sheet.

prompts.purpose: Whole-frame root and vine continuity revision
prompts.prompt: Repair only the botanical growth continuity in this FIFTEEN-frame reverse-closing sprite sheet. Preserve the exact 5-column x 3-row grid and the existing complete white flower paintings: all white petals, the central front petal folding into the narrow front panel, golden seed, sprout and adult body scale must stay as drawn. Keep the true transparent background. Frames are zero-based left-to-right, top-to-bottom. It is a REVERSE sequence, open mature flower in frame 0 to completely closed bud with four basal leaves in frame 14. The current problem is that the two curled vine stems and the little root heart remain fully grown through frame 13 and disappear suddenly at 14. Repaint complete affected drawings in frames 5-14 so these plant parts physically retract toward the central root in small steps, not vanish or fade. The vine heads must progressively move toward their central attachment as the stems shorten: frame 5 about 90 percent mature length; frame 6 80 percent; frame 7 70 percent; frame 8 60 percent; frame 9 50 percent; frame 10 40 percent; frame 11 30 percent; frame 12 20 percent; frame 13 only TWO TINY CURLED GREEN SHOOTS right beside the central root, tucked between the basal leaves, with no outside vine heads; frame 14 no visible vine shoots. The stems remain visibly connected to the base in every drawing. At the same time, gradually reduce the little separate white heart at the lowest root: full size in 0-8, 80 percent in 9, 65 percent in 10, 45 percent in 11, 25 percent in 12, a tiny folded ivory tip at the root in 13, and absent in 14. Gradually tuck the extra small green basal leaves into the root in frames 10-14, ending with the exact four-leaf closed bud already drawn in 14. Keep every remaining element fully opaque and completely painted, with natural contours and complete overlaps. Absolutely no transparent overlays, crossfade, dissolves, clipping or cut-and-paste layers. These are actual fully drawn animation frames, not a diagram. Do not change the white flower body, framing, positions or scales to accomplish the stem shortening. No text, numbers, borders, grid lines, haze, shadows or background. Output the entire repaired fifteen-frame sheet.
